questions.question_text:
Draw a population pyramid for:
a) an ageing population
b) a youthful population.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Sketch population structures.
keywords_required: a) Ageing pyramid: Narrow base (low birth rate), wide top (long life expectancy), steep/vertical sides.
b) Youthful pyramid: Very wide base (high birth rate), rapidly narrowing to a pointed top (high death rate / low life expectancy).

questions.question_text: Give some examples of factors that could cause 'indentations' on a population pyramid.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2: Interpret anomalies in population pyramids.
keywords_required: A war/conflict (causing high death rates in specific age/sex groups, usually young men).
Out-migration (emigration) of young adults seeking work elsewhere.
A sudden drop in birth rates due to government policy (e.g. anti-natalist policy).

questions.question_text:
RECALL AND CONNECT 2:
a) Define the following key terms: Evaporation, Transpiration, Interception, Percolation, Saltation, Traction.
b) Using labelled diagrams, explain the formation of a waterfall.
c) Identify two hazards of living near a river.

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1 and AO2: Cross-topic river questions.
keywords_required: a) Evaporation: water turning to gas. Transpiration: water lost from plant leaves. Interception: precipitation caught by leaves/branches. Percolation: water moving deep into rock. Saltation: pebbles bouncing along river bed. Traction: large boulders rolling along river bed.
b) Waterfall formation involves hard rock over soft rock, differential erosion (hydraulic action/abrasion), undercutting, collapse, and plunge pool formation.
c) Flooding (damage to property/crops) and waterborne diseases.
A population where the proportion of older people (usually 65+) is increasing relative to other age groups.
The composition of a population, usually broken down by age and sex.
The difference between the birth rate and the death rate (when birth rate is higher).
